focus.jbig: War headlines + rate-hike fear reset the tape · two boarded, but stand down
focus.jtag: U.S. strikes Iran around Hormuz, oil ~$90, 10Y at 20-month high, VIX popping
focus.jnote: The environment is hostile on two fronts. The U.S. and Iran are in an active exchange around the Strait of Hormuz — the U.S. launched fresh strikes on Iranian targets, which Trump said were retaliation for mine-laying and an earlier attack on a U.S. base, and Iran said it had already responded by targeting U.S. bases in the region and firing missiles toward Jordan. Crude is holding near ~$90 WTI (Brent ~$95, a near six-week high), and the surge fed inflation fear that drove the 10-year yield to ~4.81%, its highest since January 2025. Markets now price a ~70% chance of a September Fed rate hike after Chair Warsh’s hawkish Jackson Hole remarks, with ADP due today and NFP Friday. The VIX popped ~9.5% to ~16.3 and gold slid ~2.9% toward $4,325 as real yields and the dollar firmed. This is a live conflict stacked on a hawkish-Fed macro tape — exactly what a Sniper does not sell premium into.
focus.notdown: Energy (XLE, XOM, CVX, MPC) and Defense are the groups catching a bid — oil-supply fear lifts energy and conflict-demand lifts defense. Agriculture (DBA) also broke to a new 52-week high on inflation/commodity flows. But these are two-sided war trades: one de-escalation or Hormuz-reopening headline gaps crude back down and takes energy — and likely soft commodities — with it. Watch, size small.
focus.notup: Chips & high-beta tech (Nasdaq −1.03% Tue) and rate-sensitive growth are pressured by the yield spike, and CRDO gapped down ~10% post-earnings despite an EPS beat. But selling bear calls into a headline-driven, hike-fear tape carries violent squeeze risk on any peace or dovish surprise — the disciplined answer is to sell nothing new today and confirm liquidity before touching anything.
focus.why: Why RED? Composite 72 is in HOT and P(≥1% gap) at 44% is well above the 35% trigger — either alone locks out GREEN. More important than the numbers: an active military exchange with an oil shock, a 20-month-high 10Y, and a live September rate-hike debate is an unscheduled, open-ended tail you cannot time or size around — and ADP today / NFP Friday add scheduled event risk on top. The scanner boarded two names, but both carry hard gates (DBA has an UNKNOWN next-earnings date; CRDO’s liquidity is UNVERIFIED and volume was thin). Stand down on new credit spreads. Cash is a position today.

risks: Iran retaliation — the U.S. launched fresh strikes and Iran said it already hit back at U.S. bases and fired missiles toward Jordan; Trump threatened a “much harder” response. Any strike on U.S. personnel gaps the whole tape instantly — the number-one thing to watch.

Strait of Hormuz shipping — roughly a fifth of the world’s oil moved through it pre-war; flows are already severely constrained. Any full closure sends crude and diesel vertical — the week’s biggest tail.
Oil & the 10-year — WTI near $90 feeds inflation fear; the 10Y is at ~4.81%, a 20-month high, and markets price ~70% odds of a September Fed hike. A further rate pop compounds pressure on stocks.
ADP (Wed) & Nonfarm Payrolls (Fri 9/4) — a hot jobs print stacked on the oil shock hardens the hike case; a soft print could spark a relief squeeze. Two-sided event risk into a holiday-adjacent week.
AVGO (Thu) & the AI/chip complex — Broadcom headlines the tech-heavy slate; single-stock gap risk on top of rate-sensitivity in an already-jittery Nasdaq, echoed by CRDO’s ~10% post-earnings drop.
